reviews.summary: This paper surveys perturbation spectra on a static generalized Schwarzschild–de Sitter geometry arising in f(R) gravity. The metric adds linear and logarithmic terms to the familiar background. The authors calculate scalar, electromagnetic and modeled axial gravitational frequencies using Padé-averaged WKB approximations and an analytical barrier approximation, then illustrate time evolution with finite-difference wave propagation. Selected parameter choices produce frequencies close to Schwarzschild, while varying the geometric parameters changes oscillation and damping rates nonlinearly. The sampled fundamental modes are damped. The contribution is a phenomenological map of spectral changes across this metric family. The calculation leaves the coupled polar and scalaron sectors open, so the displayed decay does not by itself establish stability of the complete modified-gravity perturbation system.
reviews.relevance_reason: A direct quasinormal-mode and black-hole-perturbation topic match, with a specialized focus on a static modified-gravity metric.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text compares two approximate frequency methods, reports WKB order diagnostics and presents time evolutions. Support is strongest for the sampled barrier modes, while low-multipole accuracy and the full coupled gravitational system require further checks.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction excerpts, WKB error discussion in Sec. IV.1, Sec. V and Sec. VI. Numerical tables and field-equation derivations were not fully checked. Results emphasize fundamental modes and omit coupled polar/scalaron dynamics. Exterior boundary conditions and full stability need independent verification. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the overtone number fixed at n=0

reviews.summary: This paper studies how dark-matter subhalos perturb arrival-time differences between strongly lensed gravitational-wave images. It simulates two galaxy-scale lens configurations with 200 realizations each, comparing point-mass subhalos with a more extended NFW population in the million-to-billion-solar-mass range. Replacing part of the smooth halo with substructure produces delay shifts of hours, sometimes approaching a day in the NFW cusp example. No additional milli-images appear in the sampled standard-NFW populations, with image-finding checks using Lenstronomy. The contribution is a quantitative warning that realistic substructure can affect gravitational-wave lens time-delay modeling even without creating extra images. The results remain conditional on two lenses and specified populations, and the comparison changes both internal density profiles and spatial distributions.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly combines gravitational lensing, gravitational waves and dark-matter substructure, including timing observables relevant to lens searches.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text specifies a Monte Carlo population model, conserves the smooth/subhalo mass allocation and cross-checks image finding. However, density-profile and spatial-distribution effects are confounded, and two configurations do not establish a general milli-image probability.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, portions of Secs. II and IV.2, and Secs. V–VI. Only two macro-lenses and 200 realizations per lens are studied. A simplified additional-potential delay estimate is used, and the inspected text does not establish a full macro-model refit or detector-level inference. Figures were not visually inspected; simulations and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: Additional examination of these models will be required to isolate the effects of the density profile and spatial distribution.

reviews.summary: This paper develops a two-dimensional physics-informed neural-network solver for gravitational Kerr quasinormal modes without imposing radial–angular separation. It represents the regular Teukolsky field on a hyperboloidal domain, follows mode branches through spin continuation and refines trained frequencies with a residual-based Gauss–Newton solve. The authors report 112 frequencies across five fundamental branches and two overtones, reaching spin 0.9998. Comparisons with continued-fraction references give component errors below 0.23 percent, with larger damping errors near extremality. Network-size and hardware-repeat checks provide additional diagnostics. The contribution is a coordinate-space prototype for future nonseparable perturbation problems. Its demonstrated performance concerns Kerr, while applications to genuinely nonseparable backgrounds still require adapted regularity conditions and independent error certification.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly central to Teukolsky methods, Kerr quasinormal modes and multidimensional black-hole perturbation theory.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text reports reference comparisons over several branches and spins, independent residual-point checks, network-size comparisons and hardware repeats. Its limits on reference-free error estimates and transfer to nonseparable backgrounds are explicit.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, pipeline and diagnostic excerpts, and Sec. V. Detailed optimization appendices and all numerical tables were not checked. Training cost, branch tracking and near-extremal damping remain limitations, and independent error certification is incomplete. Figures were not visually inspected; code was not run and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the lack of an error estimate independent of reference values

reviews.summary: This paper reports a first-order Kerr metric perturbation designed to supply the input needed for second-order self-force calculations. For circular equatorial point-mass orbits, it combines a Lorenz gauge near the particle with a near Bondi–Sachs gauge at large radius, including mass and angular-momentum perturbations. The abstract describes reconstruction from separable Teukolsky-type equations solved spectrally on hyperboloidal slices. A puncture treatment addresses slow harmonic convergence near the particle and reportedly yields m-mode data accurate to about one part in ten billion. The reported examples span spins from minus 0.9 to 0.9 and orbital radii up to 50M. The contribution is directly relevant infrastructure for second-order calculations, but the accuracy and validation claims cannot be assessed from the available abstract alone.
reviews.relevance_reason: An exceptionally direct topic match to self-force, Kerr perturbations, Teukolsky reconstruction and future EMRI waveform calculations.
reviews.quality_reason: The preparation tool provided only the abstract because the full text exceeds the review limit. Numerical accuracy, completeness and validation cannot be assessed from this source.
reviews.limitations: Only the abstract was inspected. The reported results concern circular equatorial orbits and a first-order metric intended as second-order input. Full-text methods, tests, figures and derivations were not inspected.
reviews.source: Abstract only: full text exceeds review limit

reviews.summary: This paper builds a frequency-domain m-mode Teukolsky solver for a point mass on a circular equatorial Kerr orbit. Hyperboloidal slices include the event horizon and future null infinity, while a puncture/effective-source scheme regularizes the particle and a four-domain pseudospectral method handles the two-dimensional equation. An even/odd field decomposition treats the relevant equatorial asymmetry. At orbital radius 10M and spins through magnitude 0.9, dominant outgoing fluxes agree with independent toolkit values at approximately one part in ten million. Higher-mode horizon fluxes are less well resolved, and puncture order limits convergence. The contribution is reusable numerical infrastructure aimed at second-order self-force sources, with the static mode handled alongside radiative modes. Generic-orbit and second-order calculations remain extensions.
reviews.relevance_reason: A direct match to self-force, EMRI infrastructure, hyperboloidal Teukolsky methods and Kerr perturbations.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected flux comparisons use an independent toolkit, include both spin signs and expose weakly resolved horizon modes. Worldtube and resolution diagnostics explain accuracy limitations rather than relying solely on a headline error.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, flux-comparison portions of Sec. VI, Sec. VII and opening of Appendix A. Demonstrations fix orbital radius to 10M and use circular equatorial orbits. Puncture order limits convergence and some small horizon fluxes are unresolved at baseline resolution. Figures were not visually inspected; code was not run and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: The accuracy is currently limited by the order of the puncture

reviews.summary: This study models EMRI signals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of Schwarzschild geometry. A Randers angular sector produces orbital-plane precession, while leading Finslerian corrections to orbit-averaged fluxes are combined with higher-order Schwarzschild radiation reaction. Numerical-kludge quadrupole waveforms then provide illustrative LISA mismatches and a restricted Fisher-matrix forecast. For a representative one-year signal with signal-to-noise ratio 20, the reported deformation sensitivity is of order one part per million. The contribution is a phenomenological link between modified conservative motion, approximate dissipation and accumulated waveform differences. Quantitative forecasts depend on that hybrid construction and the chosen parameter subset. A self-consistent tensor-perturbation treatment and broader parameter inference are identified as necessary developments.
reviews.relevance_reason: Connects EMRI gravitational waves, eccentricity and modified orbital dynamics, with more indirect relevance to self-force because it uses a model-specific kludge prescription.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text defines waveform comparisons, adds a five-parameter Fisher forecast and acknowledges parameter-degeneracy and radiation-model limits. Its sensitivity estimates remain conditional on a hybrid approximation.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction excerpts, mismatch and Fisher discussion, and Sec. V. The source lacks an established self-consistent tensor-wave treatment for this background. The Fisher calculation varies five parameters while fixing other angles and uses a representative source. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Introduction, discussion of the unavailable self-consistent tensor-perturbation formalism

reviews.summary: This paper studies how additional fields change both black-hole quasinormal frequencies and their excitation amplitudes. In a parametrized nonrotating framework, it combines direct integration and matrix continued fractions with time-domain evolutions, Prony extraction and least-squares fitting. For initial data in the primary sector, weak coupling produces secondary-field amplitudes at first order and feedback into the primary waveform at second order. The authors tabulate amplitude coefficients for representative coupling profiles, apply the framework to dynamical Chern–Simons gravity and examine nearly degenerate axial–polar sectors. The contribution is a description of mode content beyond frequency shifts alone. Near resonance, appreciable mixing can occur even for weak coupling, although the observable amplitude pattern depends on initial conditions, phases and the specific coupled system.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly central to quasinormal-mode excitation, resonant mixing, black-hole perturbation theory and ringdown spectroscopy.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text uses complementary frequency-domain and time-domain methods, provides a perturbative scaling explanation and cross-checks mode extraction with two fitting approaches. It also distinguishes generic weak coupling from near-degeneracy.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, portions of Secs. II.4–II.5 and Sec. IV. Results use nonrotating backgrounds and representative initial data, so amplitude coefficients need not transfer directly to astrophysical mergers. Detailed convergence tables were not checked. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the secondary field is sourced at first order in the coupling

reviews.summary: This study explores shadows and scalar quasinormal modes of a rotating metric inspired by Einstein power–Yang–Mills gravity. It generates the geometry from a static seed using a Newman–Janis construction, compares shadow observables with published Event Horizon Telescope measurements and estimates scalar frequencies with leading-order WKB methods. Direct radial integration supplies selected checks on those frequency estimates. Charge and spin generally shrink the shadow while increasing oscillation frequencies and reducing damping, with sensitivity depending on the power parameter. The contribution is a combined phenomenological survey of optical and spectral observables. Its interpretation is conditional because the rotating metric's source is established within the target field theory only at the Maxwell point, and the observational intervals omit several astrophysical uncertainties.
reviews.relevance_reason: Relevant to quasinormal spectra and strong-field optical observables, but centered on a phenomenological metric family and test scalars.
reviews.quality_reason: Direct-integration checks support the sampled scalar WKB calculations. The text explicitly acknowledges the rotating metric's uncertain field-theory source and incomplete uncertainty propagation in shadow constraints.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, end of Sec. 4, selected Sec. 5 validation and Sec. 6. For power parameter different from one, a power–Yang–Mills source is unestablished. Shadow bounds fix mass and distance and omit important systematics; test-scalar modes do not supply coupled gravitational ringdown predictions. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: End of Sec. 4, limitations of observational bounds
reviews.evidence_quote: Only the statistical EHT uncertainties are propagated

reviews.summary: This paper analyzes whether GW250114 can constrain the amplitude coupling between a quadratic ringdown mode and its parent linear mode. It fits post-peak data with the 220 fundamental, 221 overtone and 220×220 quadratic contribution, then compares the inferred coupling with numerical-relativity and perturbative predictions. The broad posterior is consistent with the tested predictions, with reported discrepancies below 1.3 standard deviations. Start-time variations, an expanded model including the 440 mode and synthetic injections probe systematic effects. The contribution is a conditional observational constraint on nonlinear mode amplitudes. Current data do not select a spin-dependent coupling prescription, and uncertainty in mode content, inclination and distance limits the inference. The injection tests show why contaminating linear modes matter for louder future events.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly relevant to nonlinear black-hole perturbation theory, quasinormal-mode amplitudes and gravitational-wave ringdown spectroscopy.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected analysis includes observed data, start-time checks, an additional-mode fit and injection tests. The coupling posterior remains conditional on fixed extrinsic parameters and the assumed quadratic contribution.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction excerpts, portions of the injection and robustness results, and Sec. V. One event and fixed distance and inclination limit interpretation. Broad consistency with theory does not resolve mode-content ambiguity. Figures were not visually inspected; the data analysis was not rerun and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the inferred coupling coefficient remains conditional on the assumed presence of the quadratic mode.

reviews.summary: This paper examines equatorial periodic geodesics around a static black-hole solution in Weyl geometric gravity. It studies how two additional metric parameters shift circular-orbit thresholds, bound-orbit regions and zoom–whirl trajectories. The authors then map selected geodesics into a flat-space quadrupole prescription to construct illustrative gravitational-wave polarizations. Changing the Weyl parameters alters burst timing, amplitude and phase through the modified orbital geometry. The contribution is a qualitative connection between a specific nonmetric background, periodic-orbit structure and waveform morphology. The waveforms keep orbital energy and angular momentum fixed over the selected orbit, so they do not establish a complete radiation-driven inspiral. The paper's observational motivation would require detector-weighted comparisons and a more complete radiation model before quantitative constraints could follow.
reviews.relevance_reason: Overlaps with EMRI orbital resonances and gravitational-wave morphology, but is primarily a qualitative study of a specific modified-gravity geometry.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected geodesic and quadrupole construction supports qualitative waveform trends within the model. Claims of measurable signatures go beyond the detector-level evidence established by these selected calculations.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, part of the Introduction, Sec. IV and Sec. V. Fixed-orbit kludge waveforms omit secular radiation reaction and a self-consistent modified-gravity wave calculation. Text searches found no mismatch, SNR or Fisher analysis to quantify the observability claim. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. IV, Numerical Kludge Gravitational Wave Radiation from Periodic Orbits
reviews.evidence_quote: the constants of motion (E,L) may be treated as fixed

reviews.summary: This paper derives how a dynamical Chern–Simons pseudoscalar couples to axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of a charged, nonrotating black hole. It tracks the resulting departure from the axial–polar spectral degeneracy of general relativity. Exterior-complex-scaled spectral calculations and shooting methods resolve different mode families, with independent baseline and convergence checks. Charge redistributes the coupling between gravitational-led and electromagnetic-led branches, and an exact degeneracy produces a square-root coupling dependence near resonance. Near extremality, selected zero-damping and photon-sphere branches respond differently. The contribution is a branch-resolved perturbative account of charge-dependent mixing and isospectrality breaking. Its predictions apply at leading coupling order in the studied background, with rotating charged configurations and static tidal response left open.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly connects quasinormal modes, resonant coupled perturbations and modified-gravity black-hole spectroscopy.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text reports field-equation reductions, an independent spectral baseline, shooting cross-checks and explicit convergence and extrapolation errors. Its table distinguishes exact relations, numerical results and asymptotic estimates.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, Secs. XIII–XIV.1 and Sec. XV. Detailed derivations and appendices were not fully checked. Coupling expansions limit the predictions, near-degenerate overtone results are partly scaling estimates, and the background is nonrotating. Figures were not visually inspected; code was not run and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: an independent shooting integration of the full three-field system reproduces them

reviews.summary: This paper predicts eccentricity distributions for EMRIs formed through two-body relaxation in nuclear star clusters. It extends existing dynamical simulations toward plunge with FastEMRIWaveforms and weights trajectories by time-dependent formation rates from loss-cone modeling. The predicted distribution peaks near eccentricity 0.2, with a substantial high-eccentricity tail and up to twenty percent above 0.5 for some central masses. Wide-origin and cliffhanger EMRIs contribute to that tail. The study also identifies large regions of the predicted low-mass population outside the examined numerical flux grid. Its contribution connects formation dynamics to waveform-model coverage requirements. The predictions concern Schwarzschild primaries and one secondary mass, while the most eccentric trajectories depend on post-Newtonian evolution outside the relativistic grid.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly relevant to astrophysical EMRIs, eccentric waveform coverage, relaxation-driven formation and environmental population modeling.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected method includes formation-rate weighting, comparisons of two integration parameterizations and explicit accounting for flux-grid limits. It clearly identifies approximations affecting the high-eccentricity tail.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, portions of Secs. II.1–II.2 and IV, and Sec. V. Only Schwarzschild primaries and 10-solar-mass secondaries are modeled. Very eccentric tracks use PN5 where accuracy is less secure, with a different plunge stopping tolerance. Figures were not visually inspected; simulations were not rerun and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: both methods give almost indistinguishable results at the precision level we require.
